title: Validation that guides
summary: Data validation stops bad entries at the door: drop-down lists from named ranges, dependent lists with INDIRECT, custom rules for duplicates and limits, and messages that tell people what’s allowed.
objectives: Make drop-down lists from a named range on a Lists sheet.
Build a dependent drop-down with INDIRECT, so the item list follows the category.
Write custom rules (no duplicates, whole numbers in a range, dates in a window) and test them in a helper column first.
Choose input messages and Stop, Warning or Information alerts, and know what validation can’t catch.

slides.h: Stop bad data at the door
p: Data validation decides what a cell will accept. Bad entries are cheapest to fix before they’re typed.
Data › Data Validation: three tabs, Settings, Input Message and Error Alert.
Set it on the input cells before anyone types.
It checks typing, not formulas: it’s for input cells.
In real life: found “Gloves”, “gloves ” and “Glove” in the order list, so his SUMIFS by category missed a third of the gloves.

slides.h: A list from a named range
p: Keep the allowed values on a Lists sheet and give them a name. The drop-down’s Source is the name, so the list is easy to find and change.
Formulas › Define Name: Categories = Lists!$A$2:$A$5.
Typing the items (Helmets,Gloves,…) works, but nobody can see or update them.
For a list that grows, make it a Table and point the name at the column: =tblCats[Category].
In real life: added a fifth category, Ear protection, by typing one cell on the Lists sheet. Every drop-down picked it up.

terms: a name, like Categories, that stands for a range of cells

p: The item list should depend on the category. Name each category’s items with the category’s name; then INDIRECT turns the text in B15 into that range.
Range names can’t have spaces: “Safety shoes” needs the name Safety_shoes, and `=INDIRECT(SUBSTITUTE(B15," ","_"))`.
In Microsoft 365, a FILTER formula on the Lists sheet can feed the list instead: Source `=$H$2#`.
If someone changes the category later, the item stays: check it with a formula.
In real life: used to pick “Gumboots” under Helmets. The dependent list made that impossible.

p: Allow: Custom takes any formula that returns TRUE for a good entry. Write it for the first cell of the selection, as if you were typing it there.
Lock what stays put ($A$4:$A$13), leave the cell itself relative (A4).
Test the formula in a spare column first: TRUE for good rows, FALSE for bad.
Names (MaxQty) make the rules readable and point across sheets.
In real life: tested the duplicate rule in column F before he set it. It found two orders numbered PO-2044 that had been paid twice.

p: An input message appears when the cell is selected, before anyone types. The error alert appears after a wrong entry, and says what is allowed.
Input message: “Pairs, 1 to 500 a line.”
Error message: say what is allowed, not just “Invalid”.
Keep both short: people read the first five words.
In real life: stopped ringing stores once the quantity cell told her the limit before she typed.

p: The alert’s Style decides whether a wrong entry can stay. Only Stop truly blocks it.
Stop is the default.
Warning and Information let wrong entries in: pair them with a check column.
Data › Data Validation ▾ › Circle Invalid Data finds what got in anyway.
In real life: uses Warning for orders above 500: big orders happen, but she wants people to think twice.

p: Validation only checks what’s typed into the cell. Pasting over a cell replaces its rule, and data that was there before the rule isn’t checked.
Validation guides people; check columns and protection catch the rest.
Lesson 1.3 protects the sheet so the rules can’t be pasted away.
In real life: pasted last month’s order list over the form and wiped every drop-down. The check columns caught it the same day.

demo.intro: Add drop-downs and rules to Rakshak’s order lines.

frames.say: **B15**: Data › Data Validation › Allow **List**, Source **=Categories**, a name for Lists!A2:A5.
**C15**: Source **=INDIRECT(B15)**. With Gloves in B15, the list shows only gloves.
The duplicate rule as a custom rule on A4:A13: `=COUNTIF($A$4:$A$13,A4)=1`.
The Error Alert tab: Stop, with a message that says what’s allowed.

lab.intro: Rakshak’s order lines are in **A4:E13**, the lists and limits on the **Lists** sheet, with names: **Categories**, one name per category (**Helmets**, **Gloves**, **Shoes**, **Vests**), **MaxQty**, **DateFrom** and **DateTo**. Add the drop-downs for a new line in row 15, then test the custom rules in the check columns.

cells.A1: Rakshak: purchase order lines, checked against the rules
cells.D15: ← pick a category, then an item

tasks.prompt: Give **B15** a drop-down of the **categories**, using the name **Categories** as the Source.
hints: The Source can be a name.
tasks.rangeMsg: Typing the categories works, but use the name (=Categories) so the list follows the Lists sheet.

tasks.prompt: Give **C15** a drop-down of the **items in the category picked in B15**.
hints: Each category’s items have a name that matches the category.
INDIRECT turns the text in B15 into the named range.
tasks.sourceHint: Use =INDIRECT(B15) as the Source, so the list follows the category.

alsoWhen.msg: That list is always gloves. Use =INDIRECT(B15), so it changes when the category does.

tasks.rangeMsg: Typing the items works for gloves only. Use =INDIRECT(B15), so the list follows the category.

tasks.prompt: Test the **no duplicates** rule in **F4:F13**: TRUE when the row’s order number appears only once in A4:A13.
hints: COUNTIF(the order numbers, this row’s number).
Lock the list, leave A4 relative, and compare with 1.

mistakes.msg: Lock the list of order numbers ($A$4:$A$13) so it stays put as you fill down.

tasks.prompt: Test the **quantity** rule in **G4:G13**: TRUE when the quantity is a whole number from 1 to **MaxQty**.
hints: A whole number equals its INT; then ≥ 1 and ≤ MaxQty.

mistakes.msg: Use the name MaxQty instead of 500, so the rule follows the Lists sheet.

tasks.prompt: Test the **date** rule in **H4:H13**: TRUE when the order date is from **DateFrom** to **DateTo**.
Farah wants orders above 500 to need a second thought, but still be allowed. Which Error Alert style?
tasks.explain: Warning asks “Continue?”, so a big order can stay after a second look. Stop would block it; Information is only a note.

why.2: Information is just a note; most people click OK without reading.
why.3: Then nobody gets a second thought.

quiz.explain: Paste brings the source cell’s validation, or none.

quiz.q: You add a rule to data that’s already there. How do you find existing bad entries?
A range name for the category “Safety shoes” can’t contain a space. What fixes the dependent list?
options: Name it Safety_shoes and use INDIRECT(SUBSTITUTE(B15," ","_"))
quiz.explain: Replace the space in the name and in the formula.

points: **Data validation** on every input: List, Whole number, Date, Text length or **Custom**.
Lists from **named ranges** on a Lists sheet; dependent lists with `=INDIRECT(B15)`.
Custom rules return TRUE for good entries (`=COUNTIF($A$4:$A$13,A4)=1`); test them in a helper column. **Stop** blocks; **Warning** and **Information** let entries through.
